answers.q1: Maven, using the wrapper. Maven is primary and is what CI uses (Gradle also exists). There is no separate install step. Run `./mvnw dependency:go-offline` to prefetch dependencies, or `./mvnw -B verify` to resolve and build.
answers.q2: ./mvnw test (tests only). CI runs the full build plus tests with `./mvnw -B verify`.
answers.q4: There is no separate lint command. Formatting (spring-javaformat:validate) and the nohttp Checkstyle check (src/checkstyle/) are bound to Maven's validate phase. CI therefore checks them by running `./mvnw -B verify`. To run only the checks, use `./mvnw -B validate`. To fix formatting, use `./mvnw spring-javaformat:apply`.
answers.q5: Generated, so don't edit by hand: target/ and build/ (build output), .gradle, and the compiled CSS in src/main/resources/static/resources/css/. Per .gitignore, every *.css there except petclinic.css is generated from SCSS by `./mvnw package -P css`, so edit the SCSS sources instead. The wrapper files (.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar, gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar, mvnw, gradlew) are vendored and shouldn't be hand-edited. There is no checked-in vendored dependency directory.
